mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 1% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both above 6-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for four consecutive months, combined with rising average hourly earnings (not directly available but implied by labor market tightness), signals a risk of wage-price spiral, which increases inflation expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 3.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the housing starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as new housing construction signals broader economic activity and investor optimism.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST changes and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample testing.
